newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - July 18.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ANGER AT ARNAULT PAY-OUT DEMAND

Financial advisers working for Guinness and Grand Metropolitan have expressed puzzlement at details of the formal proposal offered the two groups by Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods firm LVMH. Arnault presented a plan this week for an alternative to the 24bn stg merger of Guinness and Grant Met, which LVMH opposes. Under the plan, a new three-way alliance would be formed from the groups' spirits businesses. However, the details show that Arnault also expected to receive 240m stg from the new company, as well as retaining a 35 per cent stake.
-- CBI SOFTENS LINE ON SINGLE CURRENCY

Prime minister Tony Blair has been told by leaders of the Confederation of British Industry that British employers want the government to delay entry to the single European currency until the turn of the decade. The CBI approach follows an extensive consultation process among its members, which found that while there is still support for the principle of monetary union, the business community shows little enthusiasm for entry at the 1999 launch date.
-- RIVALS SIGN UP FOR BT'S INTRANET LINK

Rival electronic information companies Maid and Reuters have both signed up to British Telecom's new Intranet Complete service, which was launched earlier this week. The tie-ups will allow Maid customers to access its business information products via their own intranets, while Reuters claimed that its Business Briefing product would become 'the key news and information service available through BT Intranet Compete'.
THE TIMES
-- M&S IN 192M STG DEAL FOR 19 LITTLEWOODS STORES

As many as 1,800 Littlewoods employees are set to lose their jobs, as 19 of the retailer's largest high street stores have been sold to Marks & Spencer for 192m stg. M&S, currently undergoing an 18 per cent expansion of its UK retail chain, expects the Littlewoods stores to return to profit within three years, with group chairman Richard Greenbury calling the acquisition an 'outstanding opportunity'.
-- SPOTTISWOODE CRITICISES AIMS OF DTI'S REVIEW

UK gas regulator Clare Spottiswoode has criticised the government's planned overhaul of utility regulation, stating the key consumer and environmental measures of the plans are 'unworkable'. According to Spottiswoode, increased competition between gas, water and electricity companies will hamper government efforts to reduce prices for the poor and improve energy efficiency as the market will assume control of such domains.
-- COGNAC PRODUCERS THREATEN ACTION

Independent cognac producers have criticised Allied Domecq, Seagram and LVMH for causing massive overproduction which has led to a 'cognac lake' large enough to supply worldwide demand until 2005. As a result of the overproduction, France faces its deepest crisis in 300 years and producers will now be unwillingly compelled to destroy up to one fifth of their lands in an attempt to bring prices of the drink under control.
THE GUARDIAN
-- THORNTONS SAVOURS SWEET SUCCESS

Thorntons, the luxury chocolate shop chain, has reported a 13 per cent increase in like-for-like sales over the last year to end-June, and a 27.5 per cent increase overall, to 109m stg. The company, which has 500 owned and franchises stores, plans to open a further 100 of its own stores. Analysts are forecasting full-year pre-tax profits of 11.5m stg for October, compared to a loss of 13.8m stg last year.
-- HALIFAX AND NATIONWIDE RAISE RATES

Halifax and Nationwide, two of Britain's biggest lenders, announced increases in their rates Thursday following the quarter-point rise in base rates last week. Halifax is to raise its rate to 8.2 per cent from August 1, while Nationwide also increased its standard lending rate by half a point, to 7.85 per cent. Nationwide, Britain's biggest mutual building society, maintained that its rates were still more competitive than those of its PLC competitors.
-- REFORM HOPE FOR GAMBLING

The government is involved in talks with the gaming industry which could lead to a revival of plans from the last Conservative government for further deregulation of casinos, bingo halls and betting shops. The industry is hoping that reforms will include an increase in the number of fruit machines in casinos and betting shops - a measure which the last deregulation introduced - and in the jackpots these machines are allowed to pay out.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WOOLWORTH DISAPPEARS FROM DOWNTOWN AMERICA

The Woolworth Corporation has announced plans to close its chain of 400 FW Woolworth stores in the US, so ending the battle to turn around the loss-making chain which was established in 1879. The US chain, which is unconnected to the UK Woolworths business owned by Kingfisher, reported losses of $37m (22m stg) last year.
-- MICROSOFT SCOURS WORLD FOR EMPLOYEES

US software giant Microsoft has announced plans to increase its US workforce by 19 per cent over the next 12 months, maintaining the west coast of America as 'the centre of the universe for the software business'. The company plans to recruit 3,600 people, many of whom will come from outside the US due to a shortage of good software developers in the States.
-- MICRO FOCUS SHARES TUMBLE AS CHIEF QUITS

Shares in Micro Focus, the computer and software group, tumbled 142.5p to 17.82p on Thursday following the sudden departure of chief executive Marcelo Gumucio. His exit, just 18 months after joining the company, was apparently a reflection of the company's disappointingly slow move into information technology services and products, a source close to Gumuncio said.
